$comment: The exact software the rig runs, pinned.
Captured from the simulation VM on 6 September 2026, before it was retired.
This is a known-good set: the end-to-end plan's phases 0-8 were walked
against these versions, so a new rig starts from something that has been
seen to work rather than from whatever is current on the day.
The installers are staged on the developer machine and copied to the rig,
rather than downloaded on the rig. Two reasons: the rig may have no
internet, and a hash in this file is the difference between 'the version we
tested' and 'whatever that URL serves now'.
sha256 is empty until the file has been staged and hashed once; provisioning
fills it in and then refuses anything that does not match.
minimumBytes and mustBeSigned exist because of a real near-miss: SourceForge
answered a scripted download with a 0.1 MB Cloudflare challenge page, saved
under the installer's name. A hash alone would have pinned the wrong file
happily on first run. A size floor and an Authenticode check catch a web
page pretending to be an installer before it reaches the rig.
On staying at 5.2.1 when qBittorrent 5.2.3 is out: this run is testing
Deluno, not the client. Holding the client at the version phases 0-8 were
walked against means a failure is Deluno's. Testing the client upgrade is
worth doing, and is a different run.
$weir: Built from the sibling repository rather than downloaded:
The portable zip, not the Setup.exe: Velopack installs per-user, and the
rig's services run as a dedicated account rather than as the interactive
user, so an installer run by whoever is logged in would put Weir in the
wrong profile. Unzipping to a fixed path avoids the question.
